mainTopic: רבי יהודה's limit of סכך to the four species, binding the לולב, and whether taking through another object counts as taking.
overview: This amud finishes the ברייתא about רבי יהודה's view that סכך may come only from the ארבעת המינים. The חכמים object: the Torah says 'בסוכות תשבו', a סוכה of any material, and a פסוק in נחמיה lists olive and pine branches. רבי יהודה answers that olive and pine were for the walls, while הדס, palm and עץ עבות were for the סכך. Because he also allows roofing with boards, the גמרא concludes that the palm trunk counts as the לולב's species. A ברייתא where he allows cedar (ארז) boards is answered by showing that this 'ארז' is really הדס. The גמרא then turns to רבי מאיר, who allows tying the לולב even with a cord, and to the חכמים' rejection of his proof from the gold rings of ירושלים. רבה and רבא then argue about whether decoration or a cloth is a barrier between the hand and the לולב. רבא tries to prove that taking through another object counts from the short אזוב, but the גמרא rejects that proof because the string is attached. It then begins a new proof from ashes that fell from the tube into the trough, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages object: must someone without the four species skip the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים challenge רבי יהודה. If only the ארבעת המינים are valid for סכך, a person who cannot find them would have no סוכה. But the Torah says to sit in סוכות, meaning a סוכה made of any material.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person cannot find the four species, should he just sit and not do the מצוה? But the Torah said, 'You shall sit in סוכות for seven days.' That means a סוכה made of anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים in the ברייתא attack רבי יהודה's view that סכך must come from the ארבעת המינים. They show that his view leads to an unreasonable result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If סכך must come from the four species, someone who has none of them simply cannot do מצות סוכה. The חכמים argue that the Torah says 'בסוכות' with no material listed. That suggests any valid סכך material works, so the obligation should not depend on finding special plants.

keyTerms.meaning: The four species (לולב, אתרוג, הדס, ערבה)
Sits idle, failing to do the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the גמרא speaking in its own voice. It is the end of the ברייתא from the previous section, where the חכמים answer רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה's view (that סכך comes only from the four species) was stated on the previous amud.

phrases.english: If he did not find the four species
should he sit idle [and not fulfill the מצוה]?
But the Torah said:
'You shall dwell in sukkot for seven days'
a sukkah of any material.
phrases.notes: The verse does not restrict the material.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא מָצָא אַרְבַּעַת מִינִין יְהֵא יוֹשֵׁב וּבָטֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא on the previous amud, where רבי יהודה limited סכך to the four species.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that סכך may come only from the ארבעת המינים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a reductio. His rule would leave someone without the four species unable to fulfill a Torah obligation, while the פסוק sets no limit on material.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוק in נחמיה listing olive and pine branches
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים bring a פסוק from נחמיה (counted as part of ספר עזרא). It tells the people to bring olive and pine branches along with הדס, palm, and leafy branches to make סוכות. Olive and pine are not among the four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it says in עזרא: 'Go out to the mountain and bring olive leaves, pine leaves, myrtle leaves, palm leaves, and leaves of a thick tree, to make סוכות as it is written.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים add a second proof against רבי יהודה. The פסוק names non-species plants as materials for building סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists עלי זית and עלי עץ שמן, which are not among the ארבעת המינים, as materials 'to make סוכות'. On a plain reading, then, סוכות were built from ordinary plants as well. That would contradict רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pine (or oil tree), not one of the four species
A thick-leaved tree, identified as הדס
As it is written (in the Torah)

phrases.english: And so in Ezra it says:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is actually in נחמיה ח:טו, which was counted as part of ספר עזרא.

phrases.english: 'Go out to the mountain and bring
olive branches and pine branches
and myrtle branches and palm branches
and branches of a thick-leaved tree
to make sukkot, as it is written'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a scriptural proof that supports the objection in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That סוכות may be built from materials other than the four species.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחמיה ח:טו, which lists olive and pine branches for making סוכות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reading: olive and pine for walls, the species for roofing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how רבי יהודה reads the פסוק. The olive and pine branches were for the walls (דפנות). The הדס, palm, and leafy-tree branches were for the סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה holds: these [olive and pine] were for the walls. The myrtle, palm, and thick-tree branches were for the roofing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה against the proof from the פסוק by splitting the list into two jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's limit applies only to סכך, not to walls. So the non-species plants in the פסוק can be wall material. The roofing came only from הדס, palm, and עץ עבות, which are all among the four species (עץ עבות is הדס).

keyTerms.meaning: The roof covering of the סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה never said the whole סוכה must be made from the four species. His limit is only on the סכך. The walls can be made of anything.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
these [olive and pine] are for the walls,
myrtle branches and palm branches
and thick-tree branches are for the roofing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof from the פסוק in step 2 on behalf of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the verse by assigning different functions to different materials.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to say all five materials were used for סכך, including non-species plants.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the species materials were used for סכך. Olive and pine were for walls, where any material is valid.

steps.title: Boards as roofing prove the palm trunk counts as the לולב's species
steps.stepSummary: A משנה records רבי יהודה allowing roofing with boards. Among the four species, only the palm tree can produce boards. So רבי יהודה must hold that the palm trunk and its fibers count as the לולב's species, and the גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned: one may roof with boards, according to רבי יהודה. This shows that the fibers and trunk of the palm tree are the לולב's species. Conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא combines two of רבי יהודה's positions and draws a new conclusion: the palm trunk counts as part of the לולב's species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה limits סכך to the four species and also allows boards, the boards must come from one of those species. The only possible source is the palm trunk. This settles that סיב (palm fiber) and the trunk are considered מין לולב, which is relevant to the earlier discussion about tying the לולב with its own kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm fibers (the netting on the trunk)
The trunk of the date palm

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה holds that סכך must come from the ארבעת המינים. Because he allows boards, the palm trunk must count as מין לולב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical ruling about the palm tree: its trunk and fibers count as the same species as the לולב.

phrases.english: And we learned [in a mishnah]: one may roof with boards,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Evidently, the fibers and trunk of the date palm
are the species of the lulav,
conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יהודה's limit to species סכך (step 3) and combines it with a משנה to infer something new.
steps.raayaObject: That the palm trunk and fibers are מין לולב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which רבי יהודה permits roofing with boards.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: סיב and the palm trunk count as the לולב's species.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא has רבי יהודה permitting cedar boards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה really limits סכך to the four species. A ברייתא records him permitting cedar (ארז) boards narrower than four טפחים, and cedar is not one of the four species.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יהודה really say the four species are allowed and other things are not? But a ברייתא teaches: if one roofed with cedar boards four handbreadths wide, everyone agrees it is invalid. If they are less than four handbreadths, רבי מאיר invalidates and רבי יהודה validates. And רבי מאיר agrees that if the gap between boards equals a board's width, one puts valid roofing material in between and it is valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי יהודה allows only the four species for סכך. It cites a ברייתא where he allows cedar boards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה permits narrow ארז boards. Cedar is not among the ארבעת המינים, so this seems to contradict everything said so far about his view. The details about board width and רבי מאיר's concession are part of the ברייתא, but the key point is that רבי יהודה allows ארז.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
Leftover waste of the threshing floor and winepress, valid as סכך

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement about boards of four טפחים is not the point of the challenge. The challenge rests only on the fact that רבי יהודה permits boards made of ארז, a tree that is not one of the four species.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yehuda [really] say
the four species, yes,
something else, no?
But it was taught: if one roofed it with cedar boards
that are four handbreadths wide,
everyone agrees it is invalid.
If they are not four handbreadths wide,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר פּוֹסֵל, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir invalidates and Rabbi Yehuda validates.
And Rabbi Meir concedes

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם יֵשׁ בֵּין נֶסֶר לְנֶסֶר כִּמְלֹא נֶסֶר —
phrases.english: that if there is, between one board and the next, a full board's width,
he places waste-material between them, and it is valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַרְבַּעַת מִינִין אִין מִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basic premise behind steps 3 and 4: that רבי יהודה limits סכך to the four species.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה permits only the four species as סכך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה validating cedar boards, and cedar is not one of the four species.

steps.title: Answer: the 'cedar' in the ברייתא is really myrtle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'ארז' in the ברייתא means הדס, which is one of the four species. It relies on רבה בר רב הונא for this.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'cedar'? Myrtle, in line with רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by redefining the word ארז in the ברייתא as הדס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ארז' in the ברייתא refers to הדס, then רבי יהודה is still permitting a species material. The contradiction disappears. The next step brings the source for calling הדס a kind of ארז.

keyTerms.meaning: Myrtle, one of the four species

phrases.english: What is 'cedar'? Myrtle,
in accordance with Rabbah bar Rav Huna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ארז meant actual cedar, which is not one of the four species.
steps.terutzMaskana: ארז here means הדס, so רבי יהודה still limits סכך to the four species.

steps.title: Source: the school of רב lists myrtle among ten kinds of cedar
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא reports a teaching of בי רב: there are ten kinds of ארז. The פסוק in ישעיהו lists ארז together with שיטה, הדס, and other trees, which shows that הדס is called a type of ארז.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר רב הונא said, they say in the school of רב: there are ten kinds of cedar, as it says, 'I will place in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for its answer, showing that 'ארז' can refer to הדס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בי רב read the trees in ישעיהו מא:יט as all being kinds of ארז, and הדס is in that list. So the word ארז in a ברייתא can mean הדס. This fully protects רבי יהודה's rule that סכך comes only from the four species.

keyTerms.meaning: They say in the school of רב

steps.whatToRemember: In this סוגיא, 'ארז' can mean הדס. So רבי יהודה consistently allows only the ארבעת המינים as סכך: הדס and palm (including its trunk and boards).

phrases.english: For Rabbah bar Rav Huna said,
they say in the school of Rav:
there are ten kinds of cedar,
as it is said: 'I will place in the wilderness
the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle, etc.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו מא:יט. All the trees listed there are counted as types of ארז.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the answer in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That הדס is called a type of ארז.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בי רב's teaching of ten kinds of ארז, based on ישעיהו מא:יט.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that רבי מאיר allows tying the לולב even with a plain cord.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: even with a cord, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה, that the לולב may only be bound with its own species, is explicitly רבי יהודה's ("אין אוגדין את הלולב אלא במינו, דברי רבי יהודה"). רבי מאיר disagrees and allows any binding, even a simple cord (משיחה).

keyTerms.meaning: 'etc.', meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says
even with a cord, etc.
phrases.notes: One may bind the לולב even with a non-species cord.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of רבי יהודה's view on סכך to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a לולב may be bound even with an ordinary cord.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's proof from the gold rings of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר citing the wealthy people of Jerusalem, who bound their לולבים with gold rings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר said: There was an incident with the prominent people of ירושלים, who would bind their לולבים with gold rings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר supports his view with a real-life practice. Important people in ירושלים tied their לולבים with gold, which is not one of the species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a non-species binding were forbidden, the leading people of ירושלים would not have used gold rings. So רבי מאיר argues that any binding is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: the prominent, wealthy people of Jerusalem

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir said:
There was an incident with the prominent people of Jerusalem
who would bind their lulavim
with gold rings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּיַקִּירֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings evidence for רבי מאיר's view quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: A non-species binding is valid for a לולב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice (מעשה) of the יקירי ירושלים, who bound their לולבים with gold rings.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof: the real binding was underneath
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the gold was only decoration. Underneath it, the לולב was actually bound with its own species.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that a proof?! They would bind it with its own species underneath.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי מאיר's proof. The gold rings were just for beauty, and the real binding was made of the לולב's own species, hidden underneath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story does not show that gold works as the binding. The actual halachic binding was 'במינו' (with its own species), so the story fits the חכמים' view too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is there proof from there?!' A rhetorical rejection of a proof

phrases.english: They said to him: Is that a proof?!
They would bind it with its own species underneath.
phrases.notes: The gold rings were decoration placed over the real binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not argue that רבי מאיר's ruling is impossible.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The gold rings were decorative. The real binding underneath was of the same species.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר allows any binding for the לולב. The חכמים require a binding of its own species, and they explain the Jerusalem gold rings as mere decoration.

steps.title: רבה: leave a bare handgrip so the decoration does not block
steps.stepSummary: רבה instructs the people who prepared the ריש גלותא's לולב to leave a bare spot for the hand, so that there is no חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to those who bound the הושענא of the house of the ריש גלותא: When you bind the הושענא of the house of the ריש גלותא, leave a handgrip on it, so that there will not be an interposition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives practical instructions. When decorating the ריש גלותא's לולב, leave a clear spot where the hand touches the לולב directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that decorations wrapped around the לולב can count as a barrier (חציצה) between the hand and the מצוה object. The taking must touch the לולב itself, so a bare place must be left for the hand.

keyTerms.meaning: here, the bound bundle of the four species (the לולב)
the Exilarch, head of the Jewish community in Babylonia
a handgrip, a place for the hand
an interposition, something blocking direct contact

phrases.english: Rabba said to
those who bound the hoshana
of the house of the Exilarch:
When you bind the hoshana
of the house of the Exilarch,
leave a handgrip on it
so that there will not be an interposition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבָּה לְהָנְהוּ מְגַדְּלֵי הוֹשַׁעְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following the gold-ring decoration, the גמרא raises the practical question of whether decorations block the hand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: decorative binding can be a חציצה, so a bare handgrip must be left.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the dispute between רבה and רבא about what counts as a barrier between the hand and the לולב.

steps.title: רבא: anything added for beauty is not a barrier
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבה. Anything added to beautify the לולב does not count as חציצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Anything that is there to beautify it does not interpose.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא argues with רבה. He says no bare handgrip is needed, because decoration is not a barrier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reasons that something added to make the מצוה object beautiful becomes part of it. So it does not separate the hand from the לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: does not interpose, is not a barrier

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: כׇּל לְנָאוֹתוֹ — אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ.
phrases.english: Rava said: Anything that is there to beautify it does not interpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כׇּל לְנָאוֹתוֹ אֵינוֹ חוֹצֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבה's instruction in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: whatever beautifies the לולב is not a חציצה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רבא are two different אמוראים with similar names. רבה (רבה with a ה) wants a bare handgrip, and רבא (רבא with an א) says it is unnecessary.

steps.title: רבה: do not hold the לולב through a cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that one should not hold the לולב with a cloth, because the taking must be complete and direct.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: A person should not take the הושענא with a cloth, because we require a complete taking, and there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second ruling in the same direction. Holding the לולב through a cloth is not a proper taking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ולקחתם' (and you shall take). רבה understands this as requiring a full, direct taking (לקיחה תמה). A cloth between the hand and the לולב spoils that.

keyTerms.meaning: and there is none (that is missing here)

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
A person should not take the hoshana with a cloth,
because we require a complete taking, and there is none.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: לָא לִינְקוֹט אִינִישׁ הוֹשַׁעְנָא בְּסוּדָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבה, similar to step 11, about a different kind of barrier (a cloth).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה: taking the לולב through a cloth is not a complete taking.

steps.title: רבא: taking through another object counts as taking
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees again. Taking something by means of another object still counts as taking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Taking by means of another object is considered taking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא responds to רבה's second ruling. Holding the לולב through a cloth is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא defines 'taking' more broadly. You do not need direct skin contact; lifting the object by means of something else is still 'taking'.

keyTerms.meaning: taking by means of another object
it is called taking, it counts as taking

phrases.english: And Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לְקִיחָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר — שְׁמָהּ לְקִיחָה.
phrases.english: Taking by means of another object is considered taking.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: לְקִיחָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר שְׁמָהּ לְקִיחָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: לקיחה על ידי דבר אחר שמה לקיחה.

steps.title: רבא's source: the short אזוב extended with a string
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a משנה about פרה אדומה water. A hyssop too short to reach the water may be lengthened with a string or spindle, then dipped, and then held directly for sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say that taking by means of another object is considered taking? As we learned in a משנה: If the אזוב is short, one extends it with a string or a spindle, dips it and lifts it out, and then grasps the אזוב itself and sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets out to prove his rule. He cites a משנה about sprinkling the פרה אדומה water with a short אזוב (hyssop).
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the dipping, the person is holding only the string, not the אזוב itself. Only afterward does he grab the אזוב directly to sprinkle. The next step will show why this matters.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say this? (introducing a source)
as we learned in a משנה
hyssop, used to sprinkle פרה אדומה water
he extends it to make it long enough

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְקִיחָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר שְׁמָהּ לְקִיחָה,
phrases.english: that taking by means of another object is considered taking?
As we learned: A short hyssop
one extends it with a string or a spindle,
and dips it and lifts it out,
phrases.notes: While dipping, he holds only the string or spindle.

phrases.english: and then grasps the hyssop itself and sprinkles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא brings a source for his ruling in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: לקיחה על ידי דבר אחר שמה לקיחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (פרה) permitting a short אזוב to be extended with a string for dipping.

steps.title: Why is this allowed? The Torah requires 'taking' during dipping
steps.stepSummary: רבא sharpens the proof. The Torah says 'ולקח... וטבל' (take and dip), so the אזוב must be 'taken' while dipping. Yet here it is held only through a string.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? The Merciful One said: 'And he shall take... and dip'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a pointed question to show the strength of his proof. How can dipping by means of a string be valid if the Torah demands taking during the dipping?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links taking to dipping. The person dips while holding only the string, so the משנה would seem to break the Torah's requirement. This is a rhetorical question that pushes toward רבא's conclusion; it is not a real attack on the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and he shall take and dip' (במדבר יט:יח)

phrases.english: Why? 'And he shall take... and dip' said the Merciful One!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the משנה in step 15 seems difficult, which sets up the conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to dip a short אזוב by means of a string.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires 'taking' at the time of dipping, but here the אזוב is not held directly while dipping.
steps.confusionAlert: The important moment is the dipping, not the sprinkling. At the sprinkling he holds the אזוב directly. At the dipping, which the Torah links to 'taking', he holds only the string.

steps.title: Conclusion: taking through another object counts
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה allows it, holding through the string must count as 'taking'. This proves רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that we learn from this: taking by means of another object is considered taking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא draws his conclusion. The only way to explain the משנה is that holding through the string counts as 'taking'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires taking while dipping. The משנה allows dipping by means of a string. Therefore taking through an intermediate object is real 'taking', and the same applies to holding a לולב through a cloth.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that we learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: לְקִיחָה עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר — שְׁמָהּ לְקִיחָה.
phrases.english: Taking by means of another object is considered taking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 16 and completes רבא's proof begun in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, taking by means of another object (such as a cloth or string) counts as 'taking'. This is his inference from the short אזוב, though step 18 rejects it because the string is attached.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה requires direct, unblocked contact with the לולב (a bare handgrip, no cloth). רבא holds that decorations are not a barrier and that taking through another object still counts. He tries to prove this from the short אזוב dipped by means of a string, but the next step rejects that proof, and step 19 brings a different source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the word 'taking' (לקיחה) is defined in הלכה. The definition affects how one may hold the לולב.

steps.title: The string proof is rejected because the string is attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof. A string tied to the אזוב may count as part of the אזוב itself, so the case says nothing about holding a לולב through a cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you prove this? Maybe it is different there. Since he tied the string to the אזוב, the string is treated like the אזוב itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 15–17. It says the hyssop case is not really 'taking through another object.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that holding the אזוב by a string is 'taking through something else' and still counts. The גמרא answers that the string is tied on, so it becomes part of the אזוב. Holding the string is like holding the אזוב directly. A cloth around a לולב is not attached to it, so the hyssop case cannot prove that a cloth works.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (how do you know?). This often opens a rejection of a proof.
It is like the thing itself

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבא's rule is wrong. It is only saying this particular proof does not work. The search for a proof continues in the next step.

phrases.english: From where [is this proven]? Perhaps it is different there,
phrases.notes: Challenges the proof brought from the hyssop case.

phrases.english: since he attached it, it is like [the hyssop] itself.
phrases.notes: The tied-on string becomes part of the hyssop. A cloth is not attached to the לולב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof that step 17 concluded from the hyssop case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the hyssop with a string is rejected. רבא's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An attached string counts as part of the hyssop, so it is not truly 'another object.' A loose cloth around a לולב is different.

steps.title: A new proof from ashes that fell into the water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof for רבא's rule. If the ashes of the פרה אדומה fell by themselves from the tube into the trough of water, the water is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from here: if the ashes fell from the tube into the trough, the water is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: Having dropped the אזוב proof, the גמרא brings a new source. This step only sets up the source. The inference from it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes must be put into the water on purpose, by a person, so falling by accident disqualifies the water. The point being prepared is this: if the person deliberately tips the ashes from the tube into the water, it would be valid. That would mean placing through another object, the tube, counts as a real action of 'putting in.'

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, [learn it] from here. This introduces a replacement proof.
Tube (the hollow holder for the ashes)

steps.whyThisMatters: This source involves no attachment at all. The tube is clearly a separate object, so it avoids the weakness that sank the hyssop proof.

phrases.english: Rather, [learn it] from here:
phrases.notes: Signals a new proof that replaces the rejected one.

phrases.english: If [the ash] fell from the tube into the trough, it is invalid.
phrases.notes: The ashes must be placed in the water by a deliberate human act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 18 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that taking through another object counts as taking
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about ashes of the פרה אדומה falling from the tube into the trough
